title: Baobab Cross-Engine Object Reference v1
description: Portable authority-preserving reference to a canonical Baobab object owned by another engine. Distinct from Control Plane CanonicalEntity identity and ADR-SHARED-013 ExternalReference native-system identity.

objectType.description: Stable semantic type name within the owner engine's namespace. The pair (owner_engine_id, object_type) defines the type namespace. This base contract is intentionally extensible; domain contracts SHOULD narrow it with const/enum where a specific type is required.

objectId.description: Durable canonical domain identifier minted or governed by the owning engine. This grammar does not make the value a Control Plane CanonicalEntity ID.

referenceScope.description: Authority scope of the referenced object. Tenant-scoped references carry the authoritative Control Plane tenant_id; platform references must not invent one.

referenceMode.description: CURRENT resolves according to the owner's current object state. IDENTITY_PINNED means object_id itself names an immutable historical object/version. VERSION_PINNED means the stable object_id plus object_version identifies the historical state.

versionKind.description: How the owner identifies the referenced historical state. Consumers treat the value as opaque and must not reinterpret the owner's version semantics.

value.description: Opaque owner-defined version/revision value. It is compared and resolved according to the owning engine's semantics, not by the consumer.

owner_engine_id.description: Registered engine that owns canonical domain authority for the referenced object. This is the stable engine/service identity, not a deployment/engine_instance_id and not an external system namespace. Schema validates the canonical engineId grammar; runtime use must also establish that the engine is registered.

tenant_id.description: Required exactly when scope=tenant. A reference never grants cross-tenant access; authorisation remains a separate decision.

crossEngineObjectReference.description: Minimal portable reference. It contains identity, owner, scope and pinning semantics only; it carries no foreign domain payload, provider/native-system identity, engine instance, permission or arbitrary metadata.

pinnedCrossEngineObjectReference.description: A reference safe as the identity component of historical replay/evidence when the owning domain's immutability/version semantics are also satisfied. Domain contracts SHOULD require this form for consequential historical decisions.

currentCrossEngineObjectReference.description: A deliberately dynamic reference to the owner's current object state. It must not be silently treated as a historical snapshot.

observed_at.description: When the consumer observed or captured this reference in its own workflow.

resolved_at.description: When the owning object was last successfully resolved, if resolution occurred. This is observation metadata, not part of object identity or version.

crossEngineReferenceObservation.description: Consumer-side observation metadata wrapped around a reference. Keeping time outside the identity value prevents resolution timestamps from becoming false identity/version semantics.
